previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for fever, shortness of breath, and productive cough. She was evaluated for possible pneumonia and cardiac ischemia due to new ST changes on ECG, but serial troponins remained stable within her baseline. A chest X-ray showed mild volume overload, and a small possible infiltrate was noted. She was treated with levofloxacin for community-acquired pneumonia. Her symptoms improved during the stay, and she remained hemodynamically stable. She also had transiently elevated liver enzymes, which trended downward without intervention, and an ultrasound revealed no acute abdominal pathology. She was discharged home on a short course of antibiotics and adjusted doses of lisinopril and metoprolol, with instructions to follow up on liver function tests.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease

Brief Hospital Course:
A/P: ___ y.o. female with SLE, HTN, ESRD s/p failed renal 
transplant on HD, chronic abdominal and chest pain admitted for 
abdominal pain.

# Abdominal Pain: Patient has a history of abdominal pain of 
unclear etiology, in the past attributed to partial small bowel 
obstruction as well as epiploic appendagitis. On this admission, 
CT abdomen and pelvis with oral contrast was unremarkable except 
for stool at the hepatic flexure, and there was no evidence of 
obstruction or surgical abdomen, Transplant Surgery following. 
Nausea resolved, pain improved, and lactate normalized with IV 
dilaudid and aggressive bowel regimen, and patient transitioned 
to oral dilaudid. However, on ___, patient spiked fever  and 
increased leukocytosis with left-shift despite subjective 
improvement. Concern for C. diff in this setting, and pt started 
empirically on flagyl. CT scan of abdomen and pelvis, this time 
with oral and IV contrast, was done overnight and showed right 
kidney lesion concerning for infarct v. abscess. Review of 
imaging with by both Transplant Surgery and primary team with 
Radiology more consistent with infarct. Concern for embolus 
___ or infectious endocarditis - pt w/ known MR ___. 
atheroemboli; no evidence of afib) v. thrombus (SLE vasculitis 
v. renal artery dissection) or hypercoagulable state 
(antiphospholipid syndrome - not noted in past; suspicion per 
Dr. ___ as renal transplant rejected within 2 weeks; pt 
G1P0010 - terminated). Infarct confirmed by renal ultrasound 
with doppler (study unable to comment on thrombus or vascular 
abnormality), and flagyl stopped as no further evidence of 
infection (ruled out for C. diff). Antiphospholipid panel sent 
and pending (Heme agreed that other hypercoagulability labs were 
low-yield as more likely associated with venous clot). TTE 
without evidence of vegetation; TEE with complex aortic arch 
atheroma, possible source of emboli. As patient with h/o 
platelet dysfunction, including HIT, only started on low-dose 
aspirin as discussed with Dr. ___ Dr. ___. Decision to 
anticoagulate further with warfarin to be made pending results 
of hypercoagulability labs, to be followed up by PCP (Dr. ___ 
and pt referred to Heme (Dr. ___ or Rheum (Dr. ___ as 
needed. Pt also started on statin; baseline lipid panel and 
transaminases wnl. On discharge, abdominal pain and tenderness 
minimal and much improved, no need for dilaudid.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted for abdominal pain. You were found to have an 
infarcted area (area not being perfused with blood) in your 
right kidney on CT scan of your abdomen. We are in the process 
of working you up for a source of clot. Blood tests to check for 
increased clotting risk are pending. Transesophageal 
echocardiogram showed a plaque on your aorta; this is a 
potential source for the clot in your kidney. You will be 
discharged on aspirin but any further decision to anticoagulate 
you will be made carefully pending the results of your blood 
tests in light of your history of platelet dysfunction. You were 
also seen to have a plaque inside a major heart artery on your 
echocardiogram. This is not an ideal study to evaluate this; you 
will need follow-up with a cardiologist for outpatient cardiac 
MRI. 

- You will be discharged with a new prescription for baby 
aspirin (81 mg). Please stop taking this medication and call 
your PCP if you experience bleeding or notice black or bloody 
stools.
- You will also be discharged with a new prescription for 
simvastatin for medical management of the plaque. This 
medication sometimes causes leg cramps; please call your PCP if 
this occurs. 
- You were continued on your home medications, and you should 
take all of these as prescribed on discharge. Of note, you will 
need to take prednisone 2.5 mg for 5 more days to complete the 
taper for your recent lupus flare.

Please call your doctor or come to the ED for fevers/chills, 
worsening abdominal pain, chest pain, chest pressure with left 
jaw or left arm pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, bleeding, 
black or bloody stools, or any other concerning symptoms.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Failed renal transplant, now with fever.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, the area of increased
opacification at the left base is cleared.  No evidence of acute pneumonia or
other cardiopulmonary disease.

INDICATION:  Patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal
disease status post failed transplant on hemodialysis.  History of
cholecystectomy and hysterectomy.  Right-sided abdominal pain now with fever
and leukocytosis.

COMPARISONS:  Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT of ___ and CT abdomen and
pelvis without contrast of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images through the abdomen and pelvis were
obtained following the administration of oral and 100 cc of Optiray contrast
IV.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were generated.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:  Increased density is associated with the
mitral valve, possibly indicating calcifications.  A nodular area of the left
lung base associated with atelectasis/scar is not significantly changed from
___.  A trace amount of pericardial fluid is seen.

The liver and pancreas are unremarkable.  A small rounded hypodensity at the
upper aspect of the spleen measuring 7 x 9 mm is not significantly changed
from multiple prior studies.  The patient is post cholecystectomy.  The common
duct is unremarkable.  The adrenal glands are thickened bilaterally,
compatible with adrenal hyperplasia, as previously described.

The native kidneys do enhance with contrast.  However, new from the last
contrast- enhanced study of ___, there is segmental hypoenhancement or
lack of enhancement involving the lower pole of the right kidney, with some
preserved enhancement of a thin capsule of this kidney.  The coronal images
perhaps best demonstrate the finding, with some edema or enlargement of the
affected area of the right lower pole.  It is noted that corticomedullary
differentiation was preserved on the prior study of ___.  There is a
moderate-to-large amount of stranding inferior to the lower pole of the right
kidney which extends down the right paracolic gutter.  The findings are most
compatible with a segmental renal infarction.  The right renal vein appears
patent, and the proximal right renal artery appears patent as well, as
expected given the preserved perfusion of the remainder of the kidney.  Some
calcified atherosclerotic plaque of the abdominal aorta is noted, probably
involving the origin of the right renal artery.  The degree of atherosclerotic
disease at this locale is difficult to evaluate as the study was not tailored
for this assessment.

Tiny rounded hypodensities of the left kidney measuring less than 5 mm are not
significantly changed from prior study.  The known pyloric polyps are not
appreciated on CT (noted on recent EGD of ___. Small bowel loops are
nondilated.  The colon contains oral contrast and air. The wall of a loop of
transverse colon appears slightly prominent, but the colon is not distended in
this area.  There are several small retroperitoneal nodes which are more
numerous than normally seen but do not individually meet CT size criteria for
pathologic enlargement.  These measure up to about 7 mm and are unchanged from
___.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:  Some detail is limited by streak artifact
related to the right hip prosthesis.  Pelvic bowel loops including the rectum
and sigmoid are unremarkable.  The patient is post-hysterectomy.  No definite
adnexal abnormalities are visualized.  There is no free pelvic fluid.  No
pathologically enlarged pelvic or inguinal nodes.

BONE WINDOWS:  There are no suspicious osteolytic or sclerotic lesions.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Hypodensity and enlargement of the lower pole of the right kidney with a
moderate amount of perirenal stranding extending along the right paracolic
gutter, most compatible with a segmental renal infarction.  The main right
renal vein and artery appear patent, and the upper pole of the right kidney
remains perfused.  The findings could be related to a thrombotic or an embolic
phenomenon.  Only the inferior aspect of the heart was imaged, and there are
mitral valve calcifications noted.  The finding could be related to lupus
vasculitis, microthrombi or microemboli.  Infection as a primary etiology is
thought to be much less likely given the distribution and appearance of the
lower pole right renal lesion.

2.  Unchanged nodular opacity associated with scarring at the lower lobe of
the left lung.

3.  Trace pericardial effusion.

The findings were reviewed with Dr. ___ on the morning of ___.

INDICATION:  ___ female with end-stage renal disease, questionable
renal infarct seen on recent CT.

COMPARISON:  Abdomen CT ___.

FINDINGS:  The right kidney measures 7.9 cm in length.  A trace of perinephric
fluid is identified but there is no hydronephrosis.  No stones or solid masses
are seen in the right kidney.  The lower pole demonstrates a region of
decreased echogenicity.
Color Doppler and pulse-wave Doppler images were obtained.  Doppler waveforms
of the vascular flow in the main renal artery have a normal appearance with
sharp upstrokes.  Appropriate flow is seen in the main right renal vein.  On
color Doppler imaging there is arterial and venous flow identified within the
hilum of the right kidney although the vascular flow seen is not robust.  No
flow is detectable in the lower pole on color imaging in the region of the
decreased echogenicity.

IMPRESSION:  Small echogenic kidney with an area of decreased echogenicity in
the lower pole.  The appearance is not surprising given the patient's renal
disease.  Color Doppler demonstrates vascular flow centrally and in the upper
pole however no flow is identified where the texture change occurs in the
lower pole.  This Doppler appearance is consistent with a renal infarct as
suggested on the recent CT.
